title: Foundation 2: truthful audit-fact registry without executable membership claims
description:
Successor to the stable half of eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6 (PR #476, DESIGN_INVALIDATED).

PREMISE CHANGE (why this exists): PRs #475/#476/#477 reached DESIGN_INVALIDATED
after repeatedly producing NEW defect classes following material contract changes
and fresh full reviews. The shared root cause was not implementation quality: in
all three, unsettled concepts were GENERALIZED ACROSS THE CORPUS before their
trust boundaries had been proven by a small number of concrete
source-to-execution examples. Successor work inverts that order.

GOAL: preserve the audit metadata that survived review, as a registry of AUDIT
FACTS that explicitly does NOT yet claim executable exact membership or
zero-repeat certification. Making those claims before Foundation 1 settled is
what invalidated #476.

SALVAGE AS-IS / AFTER EXTRACTION from #476: canonical finding identities; alias
accounting (70 aliases across opus:F-*, sol:CAP-*, fable:F*, indep:*, each
resolving to exactly one row); accepted / narrowed / ambiguous /
disclosed-dependency statuses with their reasoning; generalized invariant
descriptions; source review references; owning beads; duplicate canonical-ID
validation; and the historical classification reasoning.

MUST SEPARATE, and keep separable:
  * the stable audit fact and its generalized invariant;
  * source or review provenance;
  * aliases and status;
  * owner;
  * baseline affected membership;
  * current violation membership;
  * permanent closure evidence.

EXPLICIT NON-GOALS: no executable exact membership, no zero-repeat certification,
no closure-readiness predicate. Those are Foundation 3 and are blocked on
Foundation 1. This artifact must be honest that it does not yet ground them.

DO NOT PRESUME SURVIVES: the current membership queries, the source identities,
or any zero-recurrence claim.
acceptance_criteria:
• Canonical finding identities, all 70 aliases, statuses with reasoning, invariants, provenance and owners are preserved and reviewable.
• Audit fact, provenance, alias/status, owner, baseline membership, current violation membership and closure evidence are separable fields.
• The artifact makes no executable-exact-membership or zero-repeat claim, and says so explicitly.
• Duplicate canonical IDs are rejected.

F2 KEEPS: canonical finding identities; the 70 aliases; statuses + statusReasoning;

TWO #476 FIELDS COLLAPSED BECAUSE THEY CARRIED NO INFORMATION -- worth knowing
before anyone tries to "restore" them:
- #476's typed `invariant` object was BYTE-IDENTICAL across all 68 rows (same
  kind, same five dimensions); only the locator varied and it merely repeated
  the row's own audit alias. The real per-row generalized invariant prose was
  `title`, already phrased as a durable "what must remain true" statement. So
  title -> invariant. No new prose was authored (that would be source
  invention).
- #476's `regression` had evidenceKind 'bead' and locator === owningBead in all
  68 rows. Pure duplication. Dropped.
- #476's `obligation.authority` was uniformly `audit-finding:<one of that row's
  own aliases>`, i.e. zero information beyond the alias. It became
  provenance.auditFinding PLUS a validator check that it is one of the row's
  aliases -- a real check instead of a field that looks like independent
  provenance.

THE NON-CLAIM IS MECHANICAL, NOT PROSE. validateFindingRegistry carries a
DENY-LIST (obligation, target, selector, members, baselineMembership,
membership*, underivedReason, owningDerivationBead, violation, regression,
capability*, hookSelector, queryId, expectedAfterRepair, dimensions, closure)
whose error names Foundation 3 / Foundation 4 as owner, plus strict unknown-key
rejection. A later session cannot quietly repopulate membership here without
editing the validator. The module reads ONLY the registry JSON -- no
records.json, no pack directory, no node:child_process -- and a test asserts
that on the module source.

AC2 ("...baseline membership, current violation membership and closure evidence
are separable fields") is satisfied as: retained fields are separable, AND the
doc states under its own heading that those three are DELIBERATELY ABSENT,
naming eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7 / .19.1.8 (F3) and .19.1.16 (F4) as owners. Addressed,
not ignored. Do not read AC2 as licence to add empty placeholders -- the
reviewer decision postdates it and forbids exactly that.

Canonical IDs are preserved VERBATIM because F1 cites them as read-only labels
naming prior defect classes.

=== REVIEW ROUND 1 ADDRESSED 2026-08-30 -- new head 9929e82 (was eff62bb) ===
PR #507 review at eff62bb: CHANGES REQUESTED, one blocking finding -- 'Stable audit alias
identity is no longer pinned to its canonical finding'. ACCEPTED, valid.

The defect: F2 shipped two INDEPENDENT flat rosters (CANONICAL_FINDING_IDS 68,
FINDING_ALIASES 70) checked only for set equality + uniqueness. Nothing pinned WHICH
aliases belong to WHICH canonical row, so two rows could trade aliases and validation
still passed -- the only per-row check (provenance.auditFinding in the row's OWN aliases)
moves with the swap. Regression against #476, which at head 9133201 line 273 defines
CANONICAL_ROW_ROSTER (canonicalId -> aliases[]) and compares each row's aliases to its
roster entry, sorted. Verified that precedent directly before fixing.

Fix (child eshyra-o9bd.19.1.15.2, commit e8b9b34, merged 9929e82): single exact
CANONICAL_ROW_ROSTER generated from the committed JSON; CANONICAL_FINDING_IDS and
FINDING_ALIASES DERIVED from it so the views cannot disagree; assertCanonicalRowRoster
with #476 semantics (per-row sorted alias equality + duplicate/unexpected/missing).

LESSON WORTH KEEPING: 'preserve 68 canonical IDs' and 'preserve 70 aliases' are NOT two
independent inventory facts. The reviewed fact is the ASSOCIATION between them. Set
equality on each side separately does not carry it. Any future roster/inventory work in
this family should pin the mapping, not the two populations.

Regression evidence: swap test trades indep:001 / sol:CAP-001 between audit-readiness-gate
and rule-corpus-procedures AND swaps provenance with them, so only the roster can catch it.
Teeth verified empirically: with assertCanonicalRowRoster disabled the validator ACCEPTS
the swap; restored, it rejects. Plus an order-sensitive positive pin over all 68 rows.
No existing assertion weakened (roster message keeps 'missing:'/'unexpected:' spellings).

Retained deliberately: the two trailing exactSet() calls are now subsumed by the roster
assert and cannot currently fire; kept as defence in depth, flagged to the reviewer.
